page: Microsoft Azure D192ls_v7 is a high-density, compute-oriented instance within the Dlsv7 virtual machine series. Powered by the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at up to 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 system provides 192 dedicated virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 384 GB of system memory, yielding a 2 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for compute-intensive workloads that do not demand extensive RAM per core. The processor includes a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets for accelerated vector and matrix computations.

Benchmark results highlight extraordinary multi-threaded compute and data throughput capabilities. The server achieves top-tier performance in multi-core evaluations, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 197,908.53, a PassMark CPU score of 150,927.69, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 952.09 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches 685.05 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads. It also records top-tier results in Redis SET operations (265.88 million operations per second) and static web serving throughput (157.85 GB/sec). Conversely, single-core stress-ng performance sits in the middle tier, demonstrating that aggregate parallel throughput is its primary performance asset.

The D192ls_v7 contains no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, requiring remote network-attached disks for operating system and application storage. Because of its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation, the instance provides high compute density without the cost overhead associated with higher RAM capacities. This makes it an efficient architectural choice for parallel batch processing, massive web serving layers, in-memory caching tiers, CPU-based machine learning inference, and large-scale compilation tasks.

It provides 192 dedicated virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache, Intel AMX, and AVX-512 extensions. The instance is configured with 384 GB of memory, delivering a 2 GB per core ratio, with no bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the D192ls_v7 in the top tier for multi-core stress testing, PassMark CPU computation, Redis SET operations, and high-throughput static web serving, despite middle-tier single-threaded marks. Its resource profile delivers high core density without surplus RAM overhead, making it well matched for parallel batch compute, CPU-based machine learning inference, web application clusters, and large data processing workloads.
